title: Phillies Force Game 3 as Schwarber, Harper Hit Back‑to‑Back; Bohm’s 10th‑Inning Homer Beats Braves
body:
Philadelphia’s postseason hopes were kept alive on Wednesday when a dramatic 10th‑inning home run by Alec Bohm forced a decisive Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves. The moment capped a wild second‑round wild‑card duel that saw Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper each launch solo shots in the eighth inning to erase a two‑run deficit, only for the Braves to answer with a go‑ahead run in the ninth. Bohm’s two‑out blast, his third of the season, turned a 5‑4 loss into a 5‑5 tie and sent the contest to extra innings, where the Phillies ultimately prevailed 6‑5, extending the series to its final showdown.

The game began as a classic pitch‑count battle, with both clubs trading runs early. Atlanta’s starter, rookie right‑hander Jared Shuster, kept Philadelphia’s lineup in check through the first five innings, allowing just one run on three hits. Meanwhile, the Phillies’ ace, Zack Wheeler, struggled to find the strike zone, issuing two walks and surrendering a solo homer to Braves outfielder Marcell Ozuna in the third. By the end of the fifth, the score was knotted at 2‑2, and both managers began to reach into their bullpens.

The turning point arrived in the eighth inning when Philadelphia finally broke through. After a leadoff single and a sacrifice bunt, Schwarber, who had been a quiet presence at the plate all night, belted a towering 415‑foot drive to left‑center, knotting the game at 3‑3. Just moments later, Harper—still reeling from a recent slump—snapped a 390‑foot line drive over the right‑field fence, putting the Phillies ahead 4‑3. The back‑to‑back blasts energized the crowd at Truist Park and seemed to shift momentum firmly in Philadelphia’s favor.

Atlanta, however, refused to fold. In the ninth inning, veteran reliever Nick Pivetta, who had been solid through two innings, yielded a leadoff double to Braves’ shortstop Orlando Arroyo, followed by a sac fly that tied the game at 4‑4. After a defensive misplay on a grounder by Bryce Harper allowed the winning run to score, the Braves surged ahead 5‑4, prompting a furious scramble by the Phillies to regroup.

The drama intensified in the top of the 10th. With two outs and the bases empty, Bohm stepped in as a pinch‑hitter after a string of singles failed to produce a run. On a 2‑2 count, he drove a fastball over the left‑field wall, a swing that not only erased the deficit but also forced the game into extra innings. The home run marked Bohm’s first postseason extra‑inning heroics and underscored his emergence as a clutch performer for Philadelphia, a role he has cultivated since his breakout 2023 season.

In the bottom half, the Phillies’ bullpen, anchored by veteran closer Hector Neris, shut the door on Atlanta’s final chances. Neris induced a ground‑out followed by a strikeout to clinch a 6‑5 victory, sending the series to a winner‑takes‑all Game 3 back in Philadelphia. The win also gave manager Rob Mann a critical boost, as he navigated a tight bullpen usage schedule and kept his hitters focused after the late‑inning rally.

Looking ahead, both clubs now face a pivotal crossroads. The Braves, still reeling from the loss of key reliever A.J. Minter to injury earlier in the series, will need to rely on depth and strategic bullpen management to stay alive in Game 3. For Philadelphia, the challenge will be maintaining the offensive spark that produced back‑to‑back homers and a clutch 10th‑inning blast, while ensuring Wheeler’s arm remains healthy for a potential decisive game. If the Phillies can replicate the resilience displayed in Wednesday’s marathon, they stand poised to advance to the next round and keep their postseason aspirations burning bright.
